tools.name: whatsapp_biz_businesses
tools.description: START HERE. Lists the businesses you administer, each one's WhatsApp profile status, and whether it has passed Business Verification (business_verified). Call this as the FIRST tool of any WhatsApp Business conversation — including when the user only asks what this server does or how to get started — and show the result so they can pick one; every other tool is scoped to a business_id. When showing the list, ALWAYS include the complete_profile_url link for any business with profile_complete=false — the user needs to click it to finish their profile before they can onboard a phone number. Do not just mention the profile is incomplete without giving the link. Each business also carries prerequisites_met (bool) and, when blocked, a blocked_by ("No WhatsApp developer app connected", "Developer Terms not accepted") that is already written for the user and is fine to show in the list -- print it verbatim, never abbreviated to "no app" or "no ToS". prerequisites_met=true means only that the checks this tool can make have passed. It is NOT a prediction that onboarding will succeed: later steps enforce limits and integrity checks that are invisible here. Never present it as "ready", and never tell the user a business will work. Also carried are readiness_detail and fix_url, meant for after the user picks. If the chosen business has prerequisites_met=false, relay readiness_detail and fix_url instead of attempting a tool that will be refused. When you lay the businesses out in a table, label the id column "Business ID", never just "ID". Actions: list.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Connectivity check for the WhatsApp Business Tools MCP server. Returns "pong" in response and echoes the optional input in message. Use to verify the server is reachable and the access token is accepted.

message.description: Optional message to echo back. Omit to echo an empty string.
The echoed input message, or an empty string if omitted.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_add_phone_number
tools.description: BEFORE calling this tool, call whatsapp_biz_businesses so the user can pick a business and you can check profile_complete — do NOT skip that step even if the user already told you what to do. Add a phone number to a business and start onboarding (add -> verify -> register). This creates a new WhatsApp Business WhatsApp account automatically under the chosen business. Pass the selected business_id (or omit it to auto-detect; if the user administers multiple businesses this returns the list to pick from). Creating a new account is the DEFAULT and needs no discussion: do NOT list the existing accounts, and do NOT ask the user to choose between a new account and an existing one. Only pass waba_id when the user has explicitly asked to use a specific existing account, or when retrying an add that already created one (the failure returns the waba_id to reuse). The confirmation states which account the number will land on, so the user can still redirect it there. On a very large business, creating a new account is REFUSED here. That is a limit of this tool, not one the business has reached. Adding to an account the user names still works. Do not answer "yes you can add a number" on the strength of profile_complete or prerequisites_met: those do not see this. When it is refused, say the tool cannot create an account on a business this size and that nothing is wrong with their account, then offer the two options the error carries -- name an existing account, or open the link and add it there. Do not say the business has "too many" accounts, and never give a count or a floor for how many it has.vertical is the industry the business is in, and it is required for the same reason the Category field is required in the WhatsApp signup dialog: messaging limits, template review and integrity rules are keyed on it, and a number onboarded without one is treated as uncategorised. Do NOT read the list of values to the user. Choose it from what the business is actually known to do, and state your choice in the confirmation for them to correct. A name is evidence only when it names the trade: "Brie Game Page" and "Joe's Pizza" do, "Hello world", "Acme" and "test_mcp" do not -- a placeholder, a person's name or an arbitrary brand says nothing about what is sold, and neither does a phone number. When the name does point at a trade, use it; do not make the user repeat what they have already told you. When nothing points at one, ASK what the business does -- do not put a guessed category in the confirmation and wait for them to notice it. There is NO default. OTHER is not the value for "I could not tell": it is for a business whose trade IS known and that genuinely matches none of the others. Five of the values are REGULATED -- ALCOHOL, ONLINE_GAMBLING, PHYSICAL_GAMBLING, OTC_DRUGS, MATRIMONY_SERVICE -- and must never be inferred: WhatsApp blocks messaging for them outside a short per-category country allowlist, and for ONLINE_GAMBLING that allowlist is empty, so the number can message nobody. Pick one only when the user has said in their own words that this is what the business sells, and tell them the restriction before you call. A bar is RESTAURANT, a pharmacy is HEALTH, a games studio is ENTERTAIN -- the regulated value is for when the regulated goods are the business itself.  Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter". This server has no undo: nothing here can unregister a number, remove a subscription, delete an account or reverse a write. Never offer to undo one, and never imply a call can be taken back. ONLY when the user explicitly asks to undo, reverse, remove or delete something, tell them to do it themselves: webhook changes (callback URL, verify token, subscribed fields, per-account subscriptions) on the app's WhatsApp configuration page in the App Dashboard, and WhatsApp accounts, apps and phone numbers in Business Settings. Use the exact links returned by whatsapp_biz_onboarding_status in manage_links -- do not write those URLs from memory. Do not raise any of this unless asked. If a call fails with no response at all -- a gateway error, a 502, or a timeout -- there is NO reportable id for it. support_reference and fbtrace_id only exist inside an error payload this server returned; a request id from the HTTP layer is not one and must never be offered as though it were. Say plainly that the call did not come back and that there is no reference, then CHECK whether the work happened before retrying: whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers with phone_number answers that for a number, whatever the size of the business.

phone_number.description: Phone number to add, in E.164 format.

display_name.description: Business display name shown to customers in WhatsApp.

vertical.description: The industry the business is in, as one of: AUTO, BEAUTY, APPAREL, EDU, ENTERTAIN, EVENT_PLAN, FINANCE, GROCERY, GOVT, HOTEL, HEALTH, NONPROFIT, PROF_SERVICES, RETAIL, TRAVEL, RESTAURANT, ALCOHOL, ONLINE_GAMBLING, PHYSICAL_GAMBLING, OTC_DRUGS, MATRIMONY_SERVICE, OTHER.

waba_name.description: Name for the new WhatsApp account. Defaults to the display name if omitted. Do NOT offer or ask for this when collecting inputs -- it is one more decision on the very first turn and the default is almost always right. The confirmation shows the name that will be used, and the user can ask to change it then. Set it only if the user names the account themselves, unprompted. Do NOT say "WABA name" to the user — say "account name".

business_id.description: Which business the number is added under. Get it from whatsapp_biz_businesses and have the user pick; do not guess it and do not reuse one from an earlier answer about a different business.

waba_id.description: Optional: add the number to an existing WhatsApp account instead of creating a new one. OMIT THIS BY DEFAULT: creating a new account is the normal path. Pass it only when the user explicitly named an existing account to use, or when retrying an add whose error returned a waba_id to reuse. Do not volunteer it as an option or prompt the user to pick. Omitting it under WAME creates a WhatsApp Account + Messaging Account pair instead of a single account. Accepts either half of that pair: a Messaging Account id, or the WhatsApp Account id that actually holds numbers -- the server tells them apart and resolves the pair itself.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of exactly what it will do so you can show it to the user and ask them to confirm. Only after the user explicitly says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true to actually add the number.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_get_template
tools.description: Get the full details of a WhatsApp message template the user administers (state, category, rejection reason, components). PREREQUISITE: a waba_id (use whatsapp_biz_accounts to find one) and a template_id. Actions: get. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter".

business_id.description: Optional: the business the WhatsApp account belongs to. Pass the business_id the user selected so the request is authorized against their admin access to that business.

waba_id.description: The WhatsApp business account id the template belongs to (Messaging Account under WAME; same numeric id).

template_id.description: The message template id to look up.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_manage_templates_archival
tools.description: Archive or unarchive WhatsApp message templates. Set action to ARCHIVE to hide templates from the active list, or UNARCHIVE to restore them to their previous status. Only APPROVED or REJECTED templates can be archived. Pass template_ids as a list of 1 to 100 template version ids. To find ids to unarchive, call whatsapp_biz_list_templates with status set to ARCHIVED (archived templates are hidden from the default listing). The result reports succeeded and failed (id to reason) per template, so a call can partly succeed. PREREQUISITE: a waba_id and the template_ids (use whatsapp_biz_list_templates or whatsapp_biz_get_template to find ids); pass the selected business_id so the request can be authorized. If you do not have the waba_id, call whatsapp_biz_accounts first to find or pick one. Actions: archive, unarchive. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter".

waba_id.description: The WhatsApp business account id the templates belong to (Messaging Account under WAME; same numeric id).

template_ids.description: The ids of the template versions to archive or unarchive; 1 to 100 ids. Duplicates are ignored.

action.description: ARCHIVE to archive the templates, or UNARCHIVE to restore them (case-insensitive).

business_id.description: Optional: the business the WhatsApp account belongs to. Pass the business_id the user selected so the request is authorized against their admin access to that business.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of what it will do so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true to change the templates.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_publish_app
tools.description: Check whether the developer app is published (live) and, if it is not, return the link to publish it. An app still in development mode (unpublished) may not be sent real webhooks, so it is a common reason a correctly configured and subscribed webhook produces nothing. Call this whenever the user reports missing webhooks, and as the last step of onboarding after whatsapp_biz_configure_webhooks and whatsapp_biz_subscribe_webhook. This tool does NOT publish the app: publishing is gated on checks (privacy policy URL, business verification, data-handling questions and others) that must be completed on the page behind publish_url, so the user finishes it there. Actions: check.

app_id.description: The developer app to check. Omit to use the WhatsApp-enabled app already resolved for the selected business.

business_id.description: The business that owns the app. Omit to auto-detect (asks the user if they administer more than one).

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_list_templates
tools.description: BEFORE calling this tool, make sure the user has picked a business (call whatsapp_biz_businesses if not done yet in this conversation). List the message templates on a WhatsApp account the user administers (paginated, most recently edited first). Prefer narrowing with the filters below over paging through everything -- filters are applied server-side. Deleted and archived templates are hidden unless you ask for them by status. PREREQUISITE: a waba_id (use whatsapp_biz_accounts to find one). Actions: list. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter".

business_id.description: Optional: the business the WhatsApp account belongs to. Pass the business_id the user selected so the request is authorized against their admin access to that business.

waba_id.description: The WhatsApp business account id to list templates for (Messaging Account under WAME; same numeric id).

limit.description: Max templates to return in this page (optional).

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page (optional).

status.description: Filter: review states, any-match. APPROVED, PENDING, REJECTED, PAUSED, IN_APPEAL, ... DELETED, PENDING_DELETION and ARCHIVED are excluded by default -- name one here to see it.

category.description: Filter: categories, any-match. MARKETING, UTILITY, AUTHENTICATION.

language.description: Filter: language codes, any-match, e.g. en, en_US, es.

name.description: Filter: case-insensitive substring of the template name.

content.description: Filter: case-insensitive substring of the template body text.

name_or_content.description: Filter: case-insensitive substring of EITHER the name or the body text -- use this for a general "find the template about X" search. Do not combine with name or content.

quality_score.description: Filter: delivery quality, any-match. GREEN, YELLOW, RED, UNKNOWN.

source.description: Filter: how the template was created -- manual (by the business) or auto_generated (by Meta).

since.description: Filter: only templates last edited AFTER this Unix timestamp in seconds (exclusive).

until.description: Filter: only templates last edited at or BEFORE this Unix timestamp in seconds (inclusive).

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_send_verification_code
tools.description: Send a one-time ownership code to a WhatsApp Business phone number (SMS by default, or set code_method=VOICE). Step 1 of verification: call this, ask the user for the code they received, then call whatsapp_biz_verify_phone_number with it. PREREQUISITE: whatsapp_biz_add_phone_number.

phone_number_id.description: The phone number id to send the code to. Get it from whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers if you do not have it.

code_method.description: How to send the code: SMS | VOICE. Defaults to SMS.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of the code to be sent so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true to send the code.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_onboarding_status
tools.description: Where this business is in WhatsApp onboarding, as a checklist: business profile, developer app, phone number, webhooks, account subscription, app published, payment method. Every step is a real read, so use this instead of inferring progress from earlier turns. THIS IS THE ONLY READ-ONLY WAY TO INSPECT WEBHOOK CONFIGURATION AND PUBLISH STATE. Reach for it directly whenever the user asks any of: "does app X have webhooks configured", "is my webhook set up", "is this app published", "why am I not receiving webhooks". For "which of my apps has webhooks configured" the answer is webhooks_by_app, which covers every app on the business in one call. For "is this account/number subscribed" the answer is subscriptions_by_account -- an app-level callback URL says nothing about which accounts route to it, so use that table rather than calling the subscribe tool to find out. Pass app_id to answer for a specific app, and phone_number_id when the question is about one number: subscriptions_by_account is capped, so on a business with many accounts it cannot speak for one it did not read, while phone_number_id reads that account directly. Do NOT answer those by calling a webhook tool, and do NOT tell the user no read tool exists -- this is that tool. Call it when the user asks what is set up, what is left, why something will not work, or when resuming in a new conversation with no history -- and before promising any onboarding step, so you do not send them to redo work that is already done. Each step is done, todo or unknown; unknown means the check could not run, which is NOT the same as not done. Drive the first todo step. Webhook delivery needs all three of Webhooks, Account subscription and App published: a callback URL alone delivers nothing, so never call webhooks working while any of the three is todo. The Webhooks, Account subscription and App published steps are per APP and describe only the app named in checked_app -- never report them as covering every app on the business. Pass app_id to check a different one. Actions: check. Public test numbers are deliberately left out of every list this server returns, and cannot be used to send. If the user asks about a test number, or about the test WhatsApp account it sits on, tell them it is for testing only: it reaches nobody except the recipients on its own allow-list, and that allow-list can only be managed on the app's WhatsApp API testing page in the Meta App Dashboard. Never offer to add a recipient to it or to send from it -- neither is possible from here.

business_id.description: The business to report on. Omit to auto-detect (asks the user if they administer more than one).

app_id.description: Optional: which app the Webhooks and App published steps should describe. Those two are per APP, not per business, and a business often has several. Omit to use the default app; the result names the app it checked in checked_app either way. When apps_on_business is more than 1 and the user asks about a specific app, re-run with that app_id rather than assuming the default covers it.

phone_number_id.description: Optional: the number whose account the Account subscription step should answer for. Pass it whenever the question is about ONE number -- it reads that account directly, so it answers yes or no definitely, while subscriptions_by_account is capped and cannot speak for an account it did not read. Required to get a definite answer on a business with more accounts than that cap.

apps_after.description: Optional: continue the webhooks_by_app list past the row cap. Pass the next_apps_after value from the previous result; its absence means there are no more. To check ONE app, pass app_id instead -- that reads it directly rather than walking pages.

accounts_after.description: Optional: continue the subscriptions_by_account list past the row cap. Pass the next_accounts_after value from the previous result to get the next page; its absence means there are no more. Only page when the user asks to see the rest -- to answer about ONE account, pass phone_number_id instead, which is one read rather than a walk through every page.

result.description: JSON-encoded checklist: steps (step, status, detail), complete, next_step, checked_app, apps_on_business, webhooks_by_app -- one row per app on the business with its own callback_configured, subscribed_field_count and published, capped with next_apps_after carrying the cursor for the next page -- and subscriptions_by_account, one row per WhatsApp account listing the apps it sends events to -- capped, with next_accounts_after carrying the cursor for the next page when one exists.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_system_user_token
tools.description: Generate a system-user access token. Token generation is a secure in-page action; returns a deep link to the Business Settings System Users page, where the user selects a system user and generates a token. No app_id needed. Always give the developer the guide_url from the response alongside the steps -- the steps are a summary of that page, and it is the source of truth they need when the UI does not match.

business_id.description: The business id to manage system users for.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_update_template
tools.description: Update (edit) the content of an existing WhatsApp message template. Replaces the template components with the ones you provide -- a body (required) plus an optional text header, footer, and buttons, exactly like create -- so pass the FULL desired content, not just the changed part (any component you omit is removed). The name and language cannot be changed. Pass category only to change it: an APPROVED UTILITY template can change to MARKETING when the category is the only change, and a template rejected for incorrect category can take the correct category. WhatsApp rejects other category changes. Otherwise omit category. Supported content matches create: a body with positional placeholders ({{1}}, {{2}}, ...) and a matching body_example for each, or named {{customer_name}} placeholders when parameter_format=NAMED with a matching body_named_example, an optional text header (which may contain a single placeholder with a header_example or header_named_example), a location header (set header_format=LOCATION; it carries no text), or an IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT or GIF header (set header_format; to keep the current sample file of a header with the same format, pass no media input, otherwise give exactly one of header_media_url, header_media_from_template_id or header_handle), an optional static footer, and optional buttons (QUICK_REPLY, URL -- static or ending in {{1}} -- PHONE_NUMBER, VOICE_CALL -- a button that starts a WhatsApp call to the business -- CATALOG on MARKETING templates, MPM -- a multi-product message button, which makes the template MARKETING, SPM -- a single-product message button with the fixed label "View" and no text, MARKETING templates only, which needs header_format=PRODUCT, COPY_CODE -- a coupon code the recipient copies, MARKETING templates only, ORDER_DETAILS -- on MARKETING/UTILITY templates only, FLOW -- which opens a WhatsApp Flow, on MARKETING or UTILITY templates, REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO -- shares the recipient's WhatsApp phone number with the business, on MARKETING/UTILITY templates, with the fixed label "Share Contact Info" (no text), as the only button and with no header or footer, and PAYMENT_REQUEST -- a Brazil Pix/Boleto/payment-link button on UTILITY/MARKETING templates). NOT supported here: carousels and other button types. For those, CALL THIS TOOL ANYWAY with what the user asked for (for example category=AUTHENTICATION): it answers with the WhatsApp Manager deep link for that user's account. Never send the user to WhatsApp Manager without that link. You can also opt the template out of click tracking on its URL buttons with cta_url_link_tracking_opted_out. Edited templates are re-submitted for review, and only templates in an editable state can be updated. You can also set the message expiry (message_send_ttl_seconds). PREREQUISITE: a waba_id, the template_id, and the template_name (use whatsapp_biz_list_templates or whatsapp_biz_get_template to find the id); pass the selected business_id so the request can be authorized. Actions: update. DELIVERY: this is also where you add, change or remove optimized delivery on a template that already exists -- a maximum delivery price, or the budget, schedule, audience or status of the campaign a campaign template delivers through -- with optimization_spec. That is the one edit where content is optional: send optimization_spec on its own and the template content is left untouched, and conversely an ordinary content edit leaves the optimization the template already has untouched. Never create a second template to change pricing. For an optimization change, check the template first -- whatsapp_biz_get_template shows its status and what it carries today -- and show the user the confirmation this tool returns, which puts what the template bills at now beside what the edit changes it to, so they approve a difference rather than a value on its own. OPTIMIZED DELIVERY -- ESTABLISH THE GOAL FIRST. Optimized delivery (a maximum delivery price, or a budgeted campaign) is set up on a template, never on an individual message. When the request only names pricing, bidding, a maximum price, a campaign, a budget or "better delivery" without saying what to do with it, ASK which of these three the user wants, in ONE question, before calling anything: (1) SET UP a template -- whatsapp_biz_create_template, with optimization_spec only if they want it; (2) OPTIMIZE a template that ALREADY exists, or change or remove the optimization it carries -- whatsapp_biz_update_template, which is also the only way to change what a template bids, never a second template; (3) USE a template that is already optimized and approved -- whatsapp_biz_send_message. Do NOT ask when the goal is already explicit: "create a template", "add a maximum price to template X", "send template X to this number" each name one, so proceed with it. Standard setup and optimization are two steps of one flow, not two different templates: the content is composed and confirmed the same way either way, and optimization is the optional optimization_spec on top. OPTIMIZATION VALUES COME FROM THE USER. Nothing here recommends them: no tool and no prompt on this server returns a suggested value for a bid, a multiplier, a budget or a schedule, and there is no default to fall back on. Never invent, infer, estimate, or carry over from another account or template a bid_amount_major, a country multiplier, a daily or lifetime budget, or a start or end time; never present one as a recommendation, a typical value or a starting point; and never state or imply what optimization will do for delivery, reach, cost per delivery or return, none of which is knowable from here. Explain instead which fields the optimization_spec on THIS tool exposes and what each one means -- for a maximum price, the bid in the account currency per 1,000 delivered messages plus optional per-country multipliers; for a campaign, the audience, the start and end times, and exactly one of a daily or lifetime budget (a lifetime budget also needs an end time), plus, when the campaign is being created with the template, the registered WhatsApp phone number it sends from (whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers) -- and ask the user for explicit values. If the user asks you to pick, say you cannot and offer the fields. PREREQUISITES, before composing a spec: the account has to be enrolled in the product being used, and a maximum price and a campaign are separate enrolments where neither grants the other; a campaign template is MARKETING with named placeholders. Collect what is missing from the user rather than calling and letting the save fail; when the account is not enrolled, the call says so and nothing is written. Whatever is supplied, show the user the confirmation this tool returns -- which separates the values they gave from the normalized and inferred ones -- and get their approval before the template is created or changed. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter".

waba_id.description: The WhatsApp business account id the template belongs to (Messaging Account under WAME; same numeric id).

template_id.description: The id of the template to update.

template_name.description: The name of the template to update; cross-checked against template_id.

business_id.description: Optional: the business the WhatsApp account belongs to. Pass the business_id the user selected so the request is authorized against their admin access to that business.

body_text.description: The new template body text. Required whenever you change the content; omit it (and every other content field) only for an optimization_spec-only edit, which leaves the content exactly as it is. With parameter_format=POSITIONAL (the default) use positional placeholders {{1}}, {{2}}, ... (numeric, in order); with parameter_format=NAMED use named placeholders such as {{customer_name}} and supply their examples in body_named_example. FORMAT RULES for the body, all enforced when the template is saved: it must NOT start or end with a placeholder -- put wording on both sides, so "Hi {{1}}, your order shipped." and not "{{1}}, your order shipped {{2}}"; two placeholders must not sit next to each other with only spaces or punctuation between them, so "{{1}} {{2}}" is rejected -- separate them with words; placeholders must stay a small share of the text (no more than about one placeholder for every three words); the body cannot be nothing but placeholders; leave at most ONE blank line between paragraphs (three or more newlines in a row is rejected); up to 1024 characters, counting each placeholder as one; and at most 10 emoji in a MARKETING body or 6 in a UTILITY body.

parameter_format.description: POSITIONAL (default) | NAMED. POSITIONAL uses numbered {{1}}, {{2}}, ... placeholders whose examples ride on body_example / header_example in order. NAMED uses {{name}} placeholders (lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores, starting with a letter, e.g. {{customer_name}}) whose examples are supplied as {name: value} maps in body_named_example / header_named_example. Do not mix the two styles in one template.

body_example.description: POSITIONAL only: example value for each body_text placeholder, one per {{1}}, {{2}}, ... in order. Required when body_text has placeholders; omit when it has none.

body_named_example.description: NAMED only: a {name: value} map giving one example for each distinct {{name}} placeholder in body_text (for example {"customer_name": "Alex"}). Required when body_text has named placeholders; omit when it has none.

header_text.description: Optional text header shown above the body. May contain a single placeholder -- {{1}} under POSITIONAL, or a single {{name}} under NAMED -- with its example in header_example or header_named_example. For a media header set header_format instead. A text header is plain single-line text: no line breaks, no emoji, no asterisks, and no *bold* / _italic_ / ~strikethrough~ / ```code``` formatting. Up to 60 characters, counting each placeholder as one.

header_example.description: POSITIONAL only: example value for the header_text {{1}} placeholder. Required when header_text contains {{1}}; omit otherwise.

header_named_example.description: NAMED only: a {name: value} map giving the example for the single {{name}} placeholder in header_text. Required when header_text contains a named placeholder; omit otherwise.

header_format.description: TEXT (default) | IMAGE | VIDEO | DOCUMENT | GIF | LOCATION | PRODUCT. LOCATION adds a location header, which carries no text (any header_text is ignored). PRODUCT adds a product header, which carries no text or file; it goes with an SPM button on MARKETING templates, and the product is chosen at send. IMAGE (jpg or png, up to 5 MB), VIDEO (mp4, up to 16 MB), DOCUMENT (pdf, up to 100 MB) and GIF (an mp4 that plays on a loop, up to 16 MB; MARKETING templates on MM Lite accounts only) keep the current sample file when the template already has a header of that format and no media input is given; otherwise they take it from exactly one of header_media_url, header_media_from_template_id or header_handle. Any other format returns the WhatsApp Manager deep link for this account; pass it rather than deciding for yourself that the request is unsupported.

header_media_url.description: For an IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT or GIF header: a public link that returns the new sample file directly. It is downloaded once and stored with the template for review.

header_media_from_template_id.description: For an IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT or GIF header: the id of a template on this account with the same header format, whose sample file is reused.

header_handle.description: For an IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT or GIF header: a file handle from the Resumable Upload API, as the public API takes in example.header_handle.

footer_text.description: Optional footer shown below the body. Static text only -- no {{n}} placeholders. Single line, no emoji, up to 60 characters.

buttons.description: Optional buttons. Supported: QUICK_REPLY, URL (static, or dynamic when the url ends with {{1}}), PHONE_NUMBER, VOICE_CALL (starts a WhatsApp call to the business; its label is optional and it takes no send-time parameter; MARKETING and UTILITY), CATALOG (MARKETING only), MPM (a multi-product message "view items" button with a connected catalogue; it makes the template MARKETING), COPY_CODE (a coupon code the recipient copies; MARKETING templates only), ORDER_DETAILS (MARKETING or UTILITY), FLOW (opens a WhatsApp Flow; identify it with flow_id or flow_name, never both; MARKETING or UTILITY), REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO (shares the recipient's WhatsApp phone number with the business; MARKETING or UTILITY; fixed label "Share Contact Info", must be the only button, and no header or footer), and PAYMENT_REQUEST (a Brazil Pix/Boleto/payment-link button; UTILITY or MARKETING; needs payment_setting). Group same-kind buttons together (all quick-reply, then all call-to-action) -- do not interleave. Limits: up to 10 buttons in total, at most 2 URL buttons, at most 1 PHONE_NUMBER button, at most 1 VOICE_CALL button, and at most 1 COPY_CODE button; a single template cannot have both a PHONE_NUMBER and a VOICE_CALL button. A CATALOG button is allowed on MARKETING templates only, needs a catalogue connected to the WhatsApp account, and carries the fixed label "View catalog" (pass no text for it); a template using one can still be sent through this server, since it needs no per-message parameter. An MPM button needs a header and a catalogue connected to the business. A template with an MPM button is MARKETING: WhatsApp changes a UTILITY template with one to MARKETING. Note: whatsapp_biz_send_message fills body values, a media, location or text header value, and URL, quick reply and copy code button values; a template whose button needs any other value at send time cannot yet be sent through these tools. ORDER_DETAILS is a payments button for a MARKETING or UTILITY template. For the account requirements, read https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/payments/payments-br/orderdetailstemplate/ and https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/payments/payments-in/orderdetailstemplate/. Its label is fixed by the account payments market -- send "Review and Pay" (the error names the exact required value if it differs). A template carrying an ORDER_DETAILS button cannot be sent with whatsapp_biz_send_message yet (it needs order details supplied at send time, which this server does not fill). A REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO button (which shares the recipient's WhatsApp phone number with the business) works on MARKETING and UTILITY templates, carries the fixed label "Share Contact Info" (pass no text for it), must be the template's only button, and cannot be combined with a header or footer; a template using one can still be sent through this server, since it needs no per-message parameter. A PAYMENT_REQUEST button is a Brazil payments button for a UTILITY or MARKETING template. For the account requirements, read https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/payments/payments-br/payment-request-cta/. Up to three may be used -- a template with one then has at most 3 buttons in total. Its label is free text; the documented wording per method is "Copy Pix code" (pix_dynamic_code), "Copy Boleto code" (boleto), and "Open payment link" (payment_link). A template carrying a PAYMENT_REQUEST button cannot be sent with whatsapp_biz_send_message, since the payment details are supplied at send time.

type.description: Button type: QUICK_REPLY | URL | PHONE_NUMBER | VOICE_CALL | CATALOG | MPM | SPM | COPY_CODE | ORDER_DETAILS | FLOW | REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO | PAYMENT_REQUEST. Other types are not supported here -- use WhatsApp Manager.

text.description: Button label shown to the user. Required for QUICK_REPLY, URL, PHONE_NUMBER, and FLOW; optional for VOICE_CALL (the call is placed to the business number regardless); omit it for CATALOG, whose label is fixed to "View catalog", for COPY_CODE, which has no caller-set label (WhatsApp fills a translated default), and for REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO, whose label is fixed to "Share Contact Info". Plain text up to 40 characters: no {{n}} placeholders (a label is fixed when the template is created and cannot be filled in per message), no line breaks, no emoji, no formatting characters. Every button in the template needs a DIFFERENT label.

url.description: For URL buttons: an https URL. It may end with a single {{1}} placeholder to make the link dynamic -- for example "https://example.com/orders/{{1}}". The placeholder must be the LAST thing in the url; one anywhere else, or more than one, is rejected. Pass url_example with it.

url_example.description: For URL buttons whose url ends with {{1}}: the VALUE that replaces the placeholder (for example "summer2023" or "A123-456"), not the whole example URL. Required when the url has a placeholder; omit otherwise.

phone_number.description: For PHONE_NUMBER buttons: the number to call, in E.164 format (e.g. +16315551010).

ttl_minutes.description: For VOICE_CALL buttons only: optional, how long the call button stays active on a sent message, as a whole number of minutes from 1440 (1 day) to 43200 (30 days). Defaults to 10080 (7 days) when omitted.

example.description: For COPY_CODE buttons: the coupon code the recipient copies. 1 to 20 alphanumeric characters. Not used by other button types.

flow_id.description: For FLOW buttons: the numeric id of the WhatsApp Flow to open. Provide flow_id OR flow_name, never both.

flow_name.description: For FLOW buttons: the name of a WhatsApp Flow on this WhatsApp Business Account, as an alternative to flow_id; it is resolved to that flow before the template is saved, and a name that matches no flow on the account is refused. Provide flow_id OR flow_name, never both.

flow_action.description: For FLOW buttons (optional): NAVIGATE (open a Flow screen) or DATA_EXCHANGE (exchange data with the Flow's endpoint).

navigate_screen.description: For FLOW buttons: the id of the Flow screen to open first, from the Flow JSON. Required when flow_action is NAVIGATE, and for most Flows when flow_action is omitted. Do not send it with DATA_EXCHANGE.

payment_setting.description: For PAYMENT_REQUEST buttons: the payment method and its details. type is one of boleto, pix_dynamic_code, or payment_link, each with its matching object -- boleto {digitable_line}, pix_dynamic_code {code}, or payment_link {uri}.

notes.description: Optional, and only for a button type that takes notes; omit it otherwise. Supply example values for any variables in the notes text.

text.description: The notes text, for a button type that takes notes. May contain variables -- positional {{1}}, {{2}}, ... (default) or named {{slot}} when parameter_format=NAMED -- which need matching example values.

example.description: POSITIONAL notes: one example value per {{1}}, {{2}}, ... in the notes text, in order.

named_example.description: NAMED notes: an example value per {{name}} variable in the notes text, as {name: value}.

booking_url.description: Optional, and only for a button type that takes it; omit it otherwise.

url.description: The URL to open. May end with a single {{1}} placeholder, in which case pass example.

example.description: The VALUE that replaces a trailing {{1}} in url (not the whole example URL).

booking_management_url.description: Optional, and only for a button type that takes it; omit it otherwise.

url.description: The URL to open. May end with a single {{1}} placeholder, in which case pass example.

example.description: The VALUE that replaces a trailing {{1}} in url (not the whole example URL).

category.description: Optional new category: MARKETING | UTILITY. Set it only to change an APPROVED UTILITY template to MARKETING (with no other change) or to correct a template rejected for incorrect category; WhatsApp rejects other category changes. Decide it from the template's CONTENT against the public category guidelines, and from nothing else: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/template-categorization -- UTILITY requires BOTH that the content is non-promotional (no promotional or persuasive intent at all) AND that it is either specific to or requested by the user (their order, account, services, or transaction) or essential/critical to them (for example user safety). Anything promotional, anything mixing utility with promotion, retargeting, and content too vague to tell is MARKETING. Omit to keep the current category.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: Optional message expiry (time-to-live) in seconds for messages sent from this template. Omit it or pass -1 to leave it unchanged; on an edit, -1 does not clear the TTL, as with the Graph API. See https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/time-to-live/. UTILITY templates accept 30 to 43200 (12 hours). MARKETING templates accept a TTL (43200 to 2592000; 86400 on Ads Manager accounts) only when the account is eligible, and otherwise the update is rejected.

cta_url_link_tracking_opted_out.description: Optional: set true to opt this template out of click tracking on its URL (call-to-action) buttons. Omit to leave the current setting unchanged.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of what it will do so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true to update the template.

optimization_spec.description: Optional. Omit it unless the user is changing how the template is delivered, and fill it only with values the user gave you: never invent or infer a price, multiplier, budget or audience. Set type=MAX_PRICE to set, change or remove the maximum a delivery may cost; set type=CAMPAIGN to change the campaign a campaign template already delivers through. Exactly one of the two objects goes with each type -- Max Price access does not grant campaign access, and a spec carrying both is refused. Sent on its own, with no content field, it changes only delivery and the template content and review status are left alone.

type.description: MAX_PRICE (the maximum price on an otherwise ordinary template) or CAMPAIGN (the campaign a campaign template delivers through).

max_price.description: For type=MAX_PRICE. Send the values to change, or reset=true to remove the maximum price entirely.

bid_amount_major.description: The new maximum price, in the account currency's MAJOR unit (dollars, not cents) per 1,000 delivered messages. A user who says "25 cents per delivery" in a USD account means 250 here. Confirm the currency and this number with the user before sending it.

bid_strategy.description: Optional: LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, which is what a maximum price means and what is used when you omit it with a bid_amount_major.

bid_country_multiplier_overrides.description: Per-country adjustments to the base price. Omit it to leave the stored ones as they are; send the EMPTY list to remove all of them; send a list to replace them wholesale (it is not merged with the stored ones, so include every country that should keep an adjustment).

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code, e.g. CA.

multiplier.description: Positive multiplier applied to the base price for that country, e.g. 0.8.

reset.description: Set true to remove the maximum price and go back to standard rates. It cannot be combined with the other max_price fields.

campaign.description: For type=CAMPAIGN. Only these fields can change on a campaign that already exists; the phone number, optimization goal, bid strategy, promoted object, delivery status and country multipliers are fixed at creation and are refused here. Send only the fields that change.

daily_budget.description: New budget per day, in the account currency's MINOR unit (cents). Give daily_budget or lifetime_budget, never both.

lifetime_budget.description: New budget for the whole run, in the account currency's MINOR unit (cents). Give daily_budget or lifetime_budget, never both.

bid_amount.description: New bid cap, in campaign units. This is NOT the Max Price bid_amount_major and is not converted from major units.

status.description: New campaign status: ACTIVE, PAUSED, ARCHIVED or DELETED.

targeting.description: New audiences. Replaces the current ones, so list every audience the campaign should send to.

custom_audiences.description: Ids of the audiences to send to. At least one is required.

excluded_custom_audiences.description: Optional ids of audiences to exclude.

adset_schedule.description: New day-parting windows. Allowed only with lifetime_budget.

start_minute.description: Minutes past midnight the window opens, 0-1439.

end_minute.description: Minutes past midnight the window closes, 1-1440, after start_minute.

days.description: Days the window applies to, 0 (Sunday) to 6.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_configure_webhooks
tools.description: Configure WhatsApp webhooks for a business. Sets the app-level HTTPS callback URL and verify token for the WhatsApp Business Account topic and subscribes the app to a default set of WhatsApp fields -- the ones this server's own tools need, not every field the app supports. Pass `fields` to choose a different set; the result lists everything the app is allowed to subscribe to. Pick the business first (business_id via whatsapp_biz_businesses). If the business has one WhatsApp-enabled app it is used automatically; if it has several, the first is used by default and you can switch when confirming. The resolved app, callback URL, and fields are confirmed with the user before anything changes. Webhook delivery needs THREE things, and this tool provides the first: (1) WHERE events go -- the app-level HTTPS callback URL and verify token, set here; (2) WHICH WhatsApp account sends them -- whatsapp_biz_subscribe_webhook, once per account; (3) the app PUBLISHED -- an app in development mode may not be sent real webhooks. Missing (1) or (2) delivers nothing, so check all three before guessing why no webhooks arrive. To CHECK the current webhook state without changing it, call whatsapp_biz_onboarding_status -- this tool OVERWRITES the callback URL, so never call it just to look. PREREQUISITE: whatsapp_biz_businesses. Actions: configure. This server has no undo: nothing here can unregister a number, remove a subscription, delete an account or reverse a write. Never offer to undo one, and never imply a call can be taken back. ONLY when the user explicitly asks to undo, reverse, remove or delete something, tell them to do it themselves: webhook changes (callback URL, verify token, subscribed fields, per-account subscriptions) on the app's WhatsApp configuration page in the App Dashboard, and WhatsApp accounts, apps and phone numbers in Business Settings. Use the exact links returned by whatsapp_biz_onboarding_status in manage_links -- do not write those URLs from memory. Do not raise any of this unless asked.

business_id.description: The business whose app to configure. Get it from whatsapp_biz_businesses.

callback_url.description: The HTTPS webhook callback URL. It must ALREADY be live and answering the GET challenge before this tool runs -- the URL is verified as it is saved, so a user with no server deployed cannot complete this step. Before asking for a URL, ask whether they already have a receiver running. If they do not, give them this ready-made one rather than naming a tunnelling service: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/set-up-whatsapp-echo-bot (a TEST endpoint -- a production app needs its own, see https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/create-webhook-endpoint).

verify_token.description: The webhook verification token your endpoint echoes back during the challenge handshake.

app_id.description: Optional: the Facebook app to configure. Get its App ID from the Meta App Dashboard, or use an app ID returned in this tool's confirmation alternatives. Omit to use the business's WhatsApp-enabled app (the first one if there are several); you can switch when confirming.

fields.description: Optional: WhatsApp Business Account fields to subscribe (e.g. messages, message_template_status_update). Omit to use this tool's default set, which covers the fields its own tools need rather than every field the app is allowed; those are ADDED to the current subscription. Passing this instead REPLACES the subscription, so include every field you want kept.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary (and, if the business has more than one app, the list of apps to choose from) so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true.

alternative_id.description: Optional: when the confirmation lists apps to choose from, set this to the app id the user picked. Requires confirm=true. Omit to keep app_id when supplied, otherwise use the first eligible WhatsApp-enabled app on the business.

result.description: Legacy JSON response retained until eval consumers migrate. The runtime emits only this field, not a duplicate configuration object.

configuration.description: Schema-backed producer contract. Not emitted on the wire until eval consumers migrate and the legacy result field is removed.

business_id.description: The business whose app was configured.

app_id.description: The resolved app whose webhook configuration was written.

callback_url.description: The HTTPS callback URL written for this app; the verify token is never returned.

fields_written_by_this_call.description: Sorted fields this call wrote, not the full current subscription.

items.description: One webhook field written by this call.

fields_written_mode.description: added when fields were omitted; replaced when the caller supplied the full desired set.

fields_allowed_on_this_app.description: Sorted allowed fields, not the fields currently subscribed.

items.description: One webhook field the app is allowed to subscribe to.

fields_note.description: Default-field and safe replacement guidance; null when fields were chosen explicitly.

verification_skipped.description: Whether callback verification was skipped on a development or Sandcastle tier; production still verifies.

delivery_checklist.description: Endpoint, per-account subscription and app-publication checklist; this tool does not read account subscriptions.

items.description: One webhook-delivery prerequisite and its follow-up guidance.

app_published.description: Whether the app is live; null when publication could not be checked.

action_required.description: Remaining delivery prerequisites; configuring the endpoint alone does not establish working webhooks.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_accounts
tools.description: List the active WhatsApp business accounts you manage under a business, or resolve the account a phone number belongs to: account_id, name, account_status. Call this to let the user PICK a waba_id instead of asking for a numeric id -- use it before any template tool (create/get/list/update/delete) when you do not already have a waba_id. Pass business_id (or omit to auto-detect) or phone_number_id (takes precedence). If the result is empty, onboard one with whatsapp_biz_add_phone_number (it creates a WhatsApp account). Public test numbers are deliberately left out of every list this server returns, and cannot be used to send. If the user asks about a test number, or about the test WhatsApp account it sits on, tell them it is for testing only: it reaches nobody except the recipients on its own allow-list, and that allow-list can only be managed on the app's WhatsApp API testing page in the Meta App Dashboard. Never offer to add a recipient to it or to send from it -- neither is possible from here.

business_id.description: The business_id returned by whatsapp_biz_businesses for the business whose accounts to list. Omit to auto-detect (asks which business if you administer several). Ignored when phone_number_id is given.

phone_number_id.description: Optional: the phone_number_id returned by whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers. Resolve the single account this phone number belongs to instead of listing a business. Takes precedence over business_id. Omit to list the business's accounts.

after.description: Optional: read the next page. Pass the next_after value from the previous result; its absence there means there are no more. Only page when the user wants the whole list -- to find ONE account, pass phone_number_id, which resolves it directly however many the business has. Omit to start at the first owned-account page (up to 25 accounts) and include the first shared-account page when available.

shared_after.description: Optional: read the next page of customers' accounts shared with this business as their partner. Pass the shared_next_after value from the previous result; the call then returns only those shared accounts. Omit to use the normal owned-account listing; the first shared-account page is included when after is also omitted.

accounts.description: Visible owned accounts on this page, or the account resolved from phone_number_id. Absent on shared-only and selection replies.

name.description: Account display name; distinct accounts can have the same name.

phone_number_id.description: The phone number whose account was resolved; present for a direct lookup.

shared_accounts.description: Customers' accounts shared with the selected partner business. Paged separately from owned accounts; may be empty with a cursor.
