tools.name: whatsapp_biz_create_template
tools.description:
Create a WhatsApp message template on an account the user manages: MARKETING or UTILITY content with optional placeholders, text, location, product or media header, footer and supported buttons. Use this for a new custom template. To change an existing template or add optimized delivery to it, use whatsapp_biz_update_template instead of creating a duplicate.

  First have the user pick a business via whatsapp_biz_businesses and an account via whatsapp_biz_accounts; pass that account as waba_id. Follow the input-field descriptions for content, examples, header media and button constraints. Choose category from content per the guidelines on the category field, never from pricing. Collect content first, then ask standard or optimized delivery (a maximum delivery price or a budgeted campaign) unless the user already chose. Standard rates apply without optimization_spec; confirm any optimization settings with the content. The optimization_spec field says when to ask for the goal and that every value comes from the user. The first call returns a confirmation summary; only after the user agrees, repeat the same arguments with confirm=true.

  AUTHENTICATION templates, carousels and unsupported component types are not created here. Call with the requested unsupported format to obtain this account's WhatsApp Manager link; never send the user there without the returned link.

  Returns the created template_id, actual review_status and category, message expiry, optional resolved optimization and next_step. WhatsApp can reject immediately or change the requested category; report those outcomes, not a blanket "submitted for review". Give manage_templates_url as a clickable link when present. Use whatsapp_biz_get_template to check later review progress. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter".

business_id.description: Optional: the business the WhatsApp account belongs to. Get business_id from whatsapp_biz_businesses and pass the user's selected business so the request is authorized against their admin access to it. Omit to derive the business from waba_id and apply the same business-access checks.

waba_id.description: The account_id returned by whatsapp_biz_accounts for the WhatsApp business account to create the template under. Templates belong to this account (called a Messaging Account under WAME; the same numeric id).

category.description: Template category: MARKETING | UTILITY. Decide it from the template's CONTENT against the public category guidelines, and from nothing else: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/templates/template-categorization -- UTILITY requires BOTH that the content is non-promotional (no promotional or persuasive intent at all) AND that it is either specific to or requested by the user (their order, account, services, or transaction) or essential/critical to them (for example user safety). Anything promotional, anything mixing utility with promotion, retargeting (marketing even when the user asked for it), and content too vague to tell is MARKETING. WhatsApp validates the declared category against the content: a template submitted as UTILITY that reads as MARKETING is approved as MARKETING, and approved templates are recategorised later by the same rules. Businesses that repeatedly categorise marketing content as utility face escalating restrictions, up to losing utility templates across their whole portfolio. Answer a direct question about what a category costs if the user asks one, but the answer must not move the category: content decides it. (AUTHENTICATION templates are not supported here -- use WhatsApp Manager.)

body_text.description: The template body text. With parameter_format=POSITIONAL (the default) use positional placeholders {{1}}, {{2}}, ... (numeric, in order); with parameter_format=NAMED use named placeholders such as {{customer_name}} and supply their examples in body_named_example. FORMAT RULES for the body, all enforced when the template is saved: it must NOT start or end with a placeholder -- put wording on both sides, so "Hi {{1}}, your order shipped." and not "{{1}}, your order shipped {{2}}"; two placeholders must not sit next to each other with only spaces or punctuation between them, so "{{1}} {{2}}" is rejected -- separate them with words; placeholders must stay a small share of the text (no more than about one placeholder for every three words); the body cannot be nothing but placeholders; leave at most ONE blank line between paragraphs (three or more newlines in a row is rejected); up to 1024 characters, counting each placeholder as one; and at most 10 emoji in a MARKETING body or 6 in a UTILITY body.

parameter_format.description: POSITIONAL (default) | NAMED. POSITIONAL uses numbered {{1}}, {{2}}, ... placeholders whose examples ride on body_example / header_example in order. NAMED uses {{name}} placeholders (lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores, starting with a letter, e.g. {{customer_name}}) whose examples are supplied as {name: value} maps in body_named_example / header_named_example. Do not mix the two styles in one template.

body_example.description: POSITIONAL only: example value for each body_text placeholder, one per {{1}}, {{2}}, ... in order. Required when body_text has placeholders; omit when it has none.

body_named_example.description: NAMED only: a {name: value} map giving one example for each distinct {{name}} placeholder in body_text (for example {"customer_name": "Alex"}). Required when body_text has named placeholders; omit when it has none.

header_text.description: Optional text header shown above the body. May contain a single placeholder -- {{1}} under POSITIONAL, or a single {{name}} under NAMED -- with its example in header_example or header_named_example. For a media header set header_format instead. Omit to create no text header; header_format may still select a media, location or product header. A text header is plain single-line text: no line breaks, no emoji, no asterisks, and no *bold* / _italic_ / ~strikethrough~ / ```code``` formatting. Up to 60 characters, counting each placeholder as one.

header_example.description: POSITIONAL only: example value for the header_text {{1}} placeholder. Required when header_text contains {{1}}; omit otherwise.

header_named_example.description: NAMED only: a {name: value} map giving the example for the single {{name}} placeholder in header_text. Required when header_text contains a named placeholder; omit otherwise.

header_format.description: TEXT (default) | IMAGE | VIDEO | DOCUMENT | GIF | LOCATION | PRODUCT. LOCATION adds a location header, which carries no text (any header_text is ignored). PRODUCT adds a product header, which carries no text or file; it goes with an SPM button on MARKETING templates, and the product is chosen at send. IMAGE (jpg or png, up to 5 MB), VIDEO (mp4, up to 16 MB), DOCUMENT (pdf, up to 100 MB) and GIF (an mp4 that plays on a loop, up to 16 MB; MARKETING templates on MM Lite accounts only) take their sample file from exactly one of header_media_url, header_media_from_template_id or header_handle. Any other format returns the WhatsApp Manager deep link for this account; pass it rather than deciding for yourself that the request is unsupported.

header_media_url.description: For an IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT or GIF header: a public link that returns the sample file directly. It is downloaded once and stored with the template for review. Omit to use header_media_from_template_id or header_handle instead. For a media header exactly one source is required; when all are omitted the request is rejected.

header_media_from_template_id.description: For an IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT or GIF header: the template id returned by whatsapp_biz_list_templates or whatsapp_biz_get_template. It must be on this account with the same header format; its sample file is reused. Omit to use header_media_url or header_handle instead. For a media header exactly one source is required.

header_handle.description: For an IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT or GIF header: a file handle from the Resumable Upload API, as the public API takes in example.header_handle. Omit to use header_media_url or header_media_from_template_id instead. For a media header exactly one source is required.

footer_text.description: Optional footer shown below the body. Static text only -- no {{n}} placeholders. Omit to create the template without a footer. Single line, no emoji, up to 60 characters.

buttons.description: Optional buttons. Supported: QUICK_REPLY, URL (static, or dynamic when the url ends with {{1}}), PHONE_NUMBER, VOICE_CALL (starts a WhatsApp call to the business; its label is optional and it takes no send-time parameter; MARKETING and UTILITY), CATALOG (MARKETING only), MPM (a multi-product message "view items" button with a connected catalogue; it makes the template MARKETING), COPY_CODE (a coupon code the recipient copies; MARKETING templates only), ORDER_DETAILS (MARKETING or UTILITY), FLOW (opens a WhatsApp Flow; identify it with flow_id or flow_name, never both; MARKETING or UTILITY), REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO (shares the recipient's WhatsApp phone number with the business; MARKETING or UTILITY; fixed label "Share Contact Info", must be the only button, and no header or footer), and PAYMENT_REQUEST (a Brazil Pix/Boleto/payment-link button; UTILITY or MARKETING; needs payment_setting). Group same-kind buttons together (all quick-reply, then all call-to-action) -- do not interleave. Omit to create the template without buttons. Limits: up to 10 buttons in total, at most 2 URL buttons, at most 1 PHONE_NUMBER button, at most 1 VOICE_CALL button, and at most 1 COPY_CODE button; a single template cannot have both a PHONE_NUMBER and a VOICE_CALL button. A CATALOG button is allowed on MARKETING templates only, needs a catalogue connected to the WhatsApp account, and carries the fixed label "View catalog" (pass no text for it); a template using one can still be sent through this server, since it needs no per-message parameter. An MPM button needs a header and a catalogue connected to the business. A template with an MPM button is MARKETING: WhatsApp changes a UTILITY template with one to MARKETING. Note: whatsapp_biz_send_message fills body values, a media, location or text header value, and URL, quick reply and copy code button values; a template whose button needs any other value at send time cannot yet be sent through these tools. ORDER_DETAILS is a payments button for a MARKETING or UTILITY template. For the account requirements, read https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/payments/payments-br/orderdetailstemplate/ and https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/payments/payments-in/orderdetailstemplate/. Its label is fixed by the account payments market -- send "Review and Pay" (the error names the exact required value if it differs). A template carrying an ORDER_DETAILS button cannot be sent with whatsapp_biz_send_message yet (it needs order details supplied at send time, which this server does not fill). A REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO button (which shares the recipient's WhatsApp phone number with the business) works on MARKETING and UTILITY templates, carries the fixed label "Share Contact Info" (pass no text for it), must be the template's only button, and cannot be combined with a header or footer; a template using one can still be sent through this server, since it needs no per-message parameter. A PAYMENT_REQUEST button is a Brazil payments button for a UTILITY or MARKETING template. For the account requirements, read https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/payments/payments-br/payment-request-cta/. Up to three may be used -- a template with one then has at most 3 buttons in total. Its label is free text; the documented wording per method is "Copy Pix code" (pix_dynamic_code), "Copy Boleto code" (boleto), and "Open payment link" (payment_link). A template carrying a PAYMENT_REQUEST button cannot be sent with whatsapp_biz_send_message, since the payment details are supplied at send time.

type.description: Button type: QUICK_REPLY | URL | PHONE_NUMBER | VOICE_CALL | CATALOG | MPM | SPM | COPY_CODE | ORDER_DETAILS | FLOW | REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO | PAYMENT_REQUEST. Other types are not supported here -- use WhatsApp Manager.

text.description: Button label shown to the user. Required for QUICK_REPLY, URL, PHONE_NUMBER, and FLOW; optional for VOICE_CALL (the call is placed to the business number regardless); omit it for CATALOG, whose label is fixed to "View catalog", for COPY_CODE, which has no caller-set label (WhatsApp fills a translated default), and for REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO, whose label is fixed to "Share Contact Info". Plain text up to 40 characters: no {{n}} placeholders (a label is fixed when the template is created and cannot be filled in per message), no line breaks, no emoji, no formatting characters. Every button in the template needs a DIFFERENT label.

url.description: For URL buttons: an https URL. It may end with a single {{1}} placeholder to make the link dynamic -- for example "https://example.com/orders/{{1}}". The placeholder must be the LAST thing in the url; one anywhere else, or more than one, is rejected. Pass url_example with it.

url_example.description: For URL buttons whose url ends with {{1}}: the VALUE that replaces the placeholder (for example "summer2023" or "A123-456"), not the whole example URL. Required when the url has a placeholder; omit otherwise.

phone_number.description: For PHONE_NUMBER buttons: the number to call, in E.164 format (e.g. +16315551010).

ttl_minutes.description: For VOICE_CALL buttons only: optional, how long the call button stays active on a sent message, as a whole number of minutes from 1440 (1 day) to 43200 (30 days). Defaults to 10080 (7 days) when omitted.

example.description: For COPY_CODE buttons: the coupon code the recipient copies. 1 to 20 alphanumeric characters. Not used by other button types.

flow_id.description: For FLOW buttons: the numeric id of the WhatsApp Flow to open. Provide flow_id OR flow_name, never both.

flow_name.description: For FLOW buttons: the name of a WhatsApp Flow on this WhatsApp Business Account, as an alternative to flow_id; it is resolved to that flow before the template is saved, and a name that matches no flow on the account is refused. Provide flow_id OR flow_name, never both.

flow_action.description: For FLOW buttons (optional): NAVIGATE (open a Flow screen) or DATA_EXCHANGE (exchange data with the Flow's endpoint).

navigate_screen.description: For FLOW buttons: the id of the Flow screen to open first, from the Flow JSON. Required when flow_action is NAVIGATE, and for most Flows when flow_action is omitted. Do not send it with DATA_EXCHANGE.

payment_setting.description: For PAYMENT_REQUEST buttons: the payment method and its details. type is one of boleto, pix_dynamic_code, or payment_link, each with its matching object -- boleto {digitable_line}, pix_dynamic_code {code}, or payment_link {uri}.

notes.description: Optional, and only for a button type that takes notes; omit it otherwise. Supply example values for any variables in the notes text.

text.description: The notes text, for a button type that takes notes. May contain variables -- positional {{1}}, {{2}}, ... (default) or named {{slot}} when parameter_format=NAMED -- which need matching example values.

example.description: POSITIONAL notes: one example value per {{1}}, {{2}}, ... in the notes text, in order.

named_example.description: NAMED notes: an example value per {{name}} variable in the notes text, as {name: value}.

booking_url.description: Optional, and only for a button type that takes it; omit it otherwise.

url.description: The URL to open. May end with a single {{1}} placeholder, in which case pass example.

example.description: The VALUE that replaces a trailing {{1}} in url (not the whole example URL).

booking_management_url.description: Optional, and only for a button type that takes it; omit it otherwise.

url.description: The URL to open. May end with a single {{1}} placeholder, in which case pass example.

example.description: The VALUE that replaces a trailing {{1}} in url (not the whole example URL).

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: Optional message send time-to-live in seconds: how long an undelivered message waits before it expires. UTILITY templates accept 30 to 43200 (12 hours). MARKETING templates accept a TTL only on eligible accounts (Ads Manager or opted-in WABAs), and the range there is 43200 (12 hours) to 2592000 (30 days). Pass -1 for no TTL. Omit the field to use the account default.

cta_url_link_tracking_opted_out.description: Optional. Applies to URL (call-to-action) buttons: set true to opt this template out of click/link tracking on its URL buttons. Omit to leave link tracking enabled (the default).

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of what it will do so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true to create the template.

optimization_spec.description: Optional. Omit it for a standard template, which is the normal case. Supply it only when the user asked for optimized delivery, and only with values the user gave you: never invent or infer a price, multiplier, budget or audience. Set type=MAX_PRICE and fill max_price to cap what a delivery may cost; set type=CAMPAIGN and fill campaign to create the template inside a budgeted, scheduled campaign. Exactly one of the two objects goes with each type -- Max Price access does not grant campaign access, and a spec carrying both is refused. Both need the account to be enrolled in that product; if it is not, the call says so and the template is not created. DELIVERY: a template created here sends at standard rates unless you pass optimization_spec, which is what makes this a Max Price or campaign-style setup rather than a standard one. Setting up the template comes first either way: collect and confirm the content, then -- if the user has not already said -- ask whether they want standard delivery or optimized delivery (a maximum delivery price, or a budgeted campaign), and only then collect and confirm the optimization_spec. OPTIMIZED DELIVERY -- ESTABLISH THE GOAL FIRST. Optimized delivery (a maximum delivery price, or a budgeted campaign) is set up on a template, never on an individual message. When the request only names pricing, bidding, a maximum price, a campaign, a budget or "better delivery" without saying what to do with it, ASK which of these three the user wants, in ONE question, before calling anything: (1) SET UP a template -- whatsapp_biz_create_template, with optimization_spec only if they want it; (2) OPTIMIZE a template that ALREADY exists, or change or remove the optimization it carries -- whatsapp_biz_update_template, which is also the only way to change what a template bids, never a second template; (3) USE a template that is already optimized and approved -- whatsapp_biz_send_message. Do NOT ask when the goal is already explicit: "create a template", "add a maximum price to template X", "send template X to this number" each name one, so proceed with it. Standard setup and optimization are two steps of one flow, not two different templates: the content is composed and confirmed the same way either way, and optimization is the optional optimization_spec on top. OPTIMIZATION VALUES COME FROM THE USER. Nothing here recommends them: no tool and no prompt on this server returns a suggested value for a bid, a multiplier, a budget or a schedule, and there is no default to fall back on. Never invent, infer, estimate, or carry over from another account or template a bid_amount_major, a country multiplier, a daily or lifetime budget, or a start or end time; never present one as a recommendation, a typical value or a starting point; and never state or imply what optimization will do for delivery, reach, cost per delivery or return, none of which is knowable from here. Explain instead which fields the optimization_spec on THIS tool exposes and what each one means -- for a maximum price, the bid in the account currency per 1,000 delivered messages plus optional per-country multipliers; for a campaign, the audience, the start and end times, and exactly one of a daily or lifetime budget (a lifetime budget also needs an end time), plus, when the campaign is being created with the template, the registered WhatsApp phone number it sends from (whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers) -- and ask the user for explicit values. If the user asks you to pick, say you cannot and offer the fields. PREREQUISITES, before composing a spec: the account has to be enrolled in the product being used, and a maximum price and a campaign are separate enrolments where neither grants the other; a campaign template is MARKETING with named placeholders. Collect what is missing from the user rather than calling and letting the save fail; when the account is not enrolled, the call says so and nothing is written. Whatever is supplied, show the user the confirmation this tool returns -- which separates the values they gave from the normalized and inferred ones -- and get their approval before the template is created or changed.

type.description: MAX_PRICE (bid a maximum delivery price on an otherwise ordinary template) or CAMPAIGN (create the template as part of a budgeted campaign).

max_price.description: For type=MAX_PRICE. The maximum the account will pay for delivery, in the account currency.

bid_amount_major.description: The maximum price, in the account currency's MAJOR unit (dollars, not cents) per 1,000 delivered messages. A user who says "25 cents per delivery" in a USD account means 250 here. Confirm the currency and this number with the user before sending it.

bid_strategy.description: Optional: LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, which is what a maximum price means and what is used when you omit it with a bid_amount_major.

bid_country_multiplier_overrides.description: Optional per-country adjustments to the base price. Include a country only when the user named it with an explicit multiplier; every other country uses the base price.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code, e.g. CA.

multiplier.description: Positive multiplier applied to the base price for that country, e.g. 0.8.

campaign.description: For type=CAMPAIGN. The template is created MARKETING with parameter_format=NAMED, and a campaign with its ad objects is created around it; if that fails the template is removed again, so there is nothing to clean up. Needs the phone number, the audience, a start time and exactly one budget.

whatsapp_business_phone_number_id.description: The registered WhatsApp phone number id the campaign sends from (use whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers to find it).

custom_audiences.description: Ids of the audiences to send to. At least one is required -- a campaign with no audience cannot be created.

excluded_custom_audiences.description: Optional ids of audiences to exclude.

start_time.description: When delivery starts, ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-07-01T09:00:00Z). Must be in the future.

end_time.description: When delivery stops, ISO 8601. Required with lifetime_budget; optional with daily_budget.

daily_budget.description: Budget per day, in the account currency's MINOR unit (cents). Give daily_budget or lifetime_budget, never both.

lifetime_budget.description: Budget for the whole run, in the account currency's MINOR unit (cents). Needs end_time. Give daily_budget or lifetime_budget, never both.

optimization_goal.description: Optional: REACH (the default), LINK_CLICKS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS or VALUE. OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS needs promoted_object.

bid_strategy.description: Optional: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (the default) or LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, which needs bid_amount.

bid_amount.description: Optional bid cap for LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, in campaign units. This is NOT the Max Price bid_amount_major and is not converted from major units.

status.description: Optional: ACTIVE (the default), PAUSED or ARCHIVED. A campaign cannot be created DELETED.

promoted_object.description: Required for optimization_goal=OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS: what conversion to optimize for. Give custom_event_type with pixel_id or application_id.

custom_event_type.description: The conversion event, e.g. PURCHASE or LEAD.

attribution_spec.description: Optional attribution windows. Allowed only with optimization_goal=OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS.

adset_schedule.description: Optional day-parting windows. Allowed only with lifetime_budget.

start_minute.description: Minutes past midnight the window opens, 0-1439.

end_minute.description: Minutes past midnight the window closes, 1-1440, after start_minute.

days.description: Days the window applies to, 0 (Sunday) to 6.

result.description: Legacy JSON response retained until eval consumers migrate. Only this field is emitted; created_template is not duplicated alongside it.

created_template.description: Schema-backed create producer contract. Not emitted on the wire until eval consumers migrate and the legacy result is removed.

template_id.description: ID of the template that was actually created, including a template immediately rejected.

review_status.description: The saved review state, such as APPROVED, REJECTED or PENDING; null when unavailable.

category.description: The actual saved category after content classification, not necessarily the requested category; null when unavailable.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: The saved message expiry in seconds; null when no expiry is configured.

optimization_spec.description: Resolved stored optimization settings; omitted for standard delivery.

type.description: The resolved optimization type: MAX_PRICE or CAMPAIGN.

account_currency.description: The account currency code, when available.

bid_amount.description: The resolved stored bid amount in minor currency units per 1,000 deliveries; omitted when no amount was resolved.

bid_strategy.description: The resolved bid strategy, when available.

bid_country_multiplier_overrides.description: Resolved country adjustments; omitted when none were resolved.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code for this price adjustment.

campaign_created.description: For CAMPAIGN: whether the campaign and its ad objects were created with the template.

supplied_fields.description: Optimization fields explicitly supplied by the caller, not inferred by the server.

items.description: Name of an optimization field supplied by the caller.

inferred_fields.description: Optimization fields inferred by the server, not supplied explicitly.

items.description: Name of an optimization field inferred by the server.

requested_category.description: The requested category, included only when it differs from the saved category.

category_changed.description: True when WhatsApp changed the category; absent when it did not change or cannot be compared.

category_change_note.description: Guidance to report a category change; omitted without a detected change.

manage_templates_url.description: Clickable WhatsApp Manager link to the account templates; omitted if the link could not be built.

rejected_reason.description: Rejection reason, included only for an immediately rejected template; null if the reason is unavailable.

next_step.description: Outcome-specific next action: fix rejection, use the approved template, or check pending review later.

model_note.description: Guidance to show the management link when present.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_create_template_from_library
tools.description: BEFORE calling this tool, make sure the user has picked a business (call whatsapp_biz_businesses if not done yet in this conversation), and pick the library template with whatsapp_biz_template_library so you have its exact library_template_name and language. Creates a real template on the user's account from a Template Library entry. The wording and the category come from the library and cannot be edited here -- that is the point: an unchanged library template can skip review. You only supply the new template name, plus values for whatever the entry asks for (button URLs and phone numbers, and any body inputs such as the business name), which whatsapp_biz_template_library returns under required_inputs. To change the wording, create the template with whatsapp_biz_create_template instead and accept the review. PREREQUISITE: a waba_id the user manages (use whatsapp_biz_accounts to find or pick one). You can optionally set a message send TTL (time-to-live) in seconds on the new template. Actions: create. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter".

business_id.description: Optional: the business the WhatsApp account belongs to. Get business_id from whatsapp_biz_businesses and pass the user's selected business so the request is authorized against their admin access to it. Omit to derive the business from waba_id and still apply the business-access checks.

waba_id.description: The account_id returned by whatsapp_biz_accounts for the account to create the template under (Messaging Account under WAME; same numeric id).

library_template_name.description: The name of the Template Library entry to create from, exactly as whatsapp_biz_template_library returned it.

language.description: BCP-47 language code of the library entry, e.g. en_US. It must be a language that entry is published in.

template_name.description: Name for the NEW template on the account. Lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores.

buttons.description: Values for the buttons the library entry defines, in the order it lists them. The button TEXT comes from the library; you supply only the URL or phone number behind it. Omit when the entry has no buttons needing input.

type.description: Button type from the library entry, as returned in its required_inputs (e.g. URL, PHONE_NUMBER, QUICK_REPLY).

url.description: For a URL button: the https URL to open. May end with a single {{1}} placeholder, in which case pass url_example too.

url_example.description: The VALUE that replaces {{1}} in url (not the whole example URL). Required when url ends with {{1}}.

phone_number.description: For a PHONE_NUMBER button: the number to call, in E.164 format (e.g. +16315551010).

body_inputs.description: Values for the named body parameters the library entry requires at creation time. Ask the user for these rather than inventing them: they become permanent text in the template. Omit to pass an empty list. Any required body values must still be supplied; missing required values are rejected, not inferred.

param_name.description: The named body parameter to fill, as listed under required_inputs (e.g. business_name).

value.description: The value to bake into the template body. This becomes fixed text -- it is NOT filled in per message, so use something constant like the business name, never a customer detail.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: Optional message send TTL (time-to-live) in seconds for the new template, as a numeric string. Pass -1 to leave it unset (the default). UTILITY templates accept 30 to 43200 (12 hours). MARKETING templates only accept a TTL on eligible accounts (Ads Manager or APIX WhatsApp accounts); for others, setting one is rejected at save.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of what it will create so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true.

result.description: Legacy JSON response retained until eval consumers migrate. Only this field is emitted; created_template is not duplicated alongside it.

created_template.description: Schema-backed library-create producer contract. Not emitted on the wire until eval consumers migrate and legacy result is removed.

template_id.description: ID of the template created from the library entry.

name.description: The actual saved name of the new template.

category.description: The actual saved template category; null if unavailable.

review_status.description: The actual saved review state, such as APPROVED, REJECTED or PENDING; null if unavailable.

message_send_ttl_seconds.description: The saved expiry in seconds; null when no message expiry is set.

library_template_name.description: The library entry used to create this template.

next_step.description: Legacy text retained byte-for-byte for eval compatibility during staging. REJECTED still has the legacy check-later text; do not treat it as pending review. Add rejection-specific guidance and a rejected_reason field before eval migration and retirement of result.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_phone_numbers
tools.description: BEFORE calling this tool, make sure the user has picked a business (call whatsapp_biz_businesses if not done yet in this conversation). List the phone numbers on a business (or a specific account): id, number, name, status. Call this to let the user PICK a number instead of asking them for a numeric phone_number_id — use it before send_message, or any tool that needs a phone_number_id, when you do not already have one. If the result is empty (no numbers yet), do NOT ask for a phone_number_id — onboard one with whatsapp_biz_add_phone_number first. To finish a half-onboarded number, follow its next_action and do NOT restart the flow: onboarding_state=verified_not_registered means the number is already verified and only needs whatsapp_biz_register_phone_number, so sending it another verification code is wrong. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter". Public test numbers are deliberately left out of every list this server returns, and cannot be used to send. If the user asks about a test number, or about the test WhatsApp account it sits on, tell them it is for testing only: it reaches nobody except the recipients on its own allow-list, and that allow-list can only be managed on the app's WhatsApp API testing page in the Meta App Dashboard. Never offer to add a recipient to it or to send from it -- neither is possible from here.

business_id.description: The business whose phone numbers to list. Omit to auto-detect (asks which business if you administer several). Ignored when waba_id is given.

waba_id.description: Optional: list the numbers on a specific WhatsApp account instead of the whole business. Takes precedence over business_id. Note: under WAME, phone numbers belong to the WhatsApp Account (not the Messaging Account), but the server resolves this internally.

status.description: Optional filter: "linked" (registered, ready to send) or "pending" (NOT registered — which covers both "not yet verified" and "verified, waiting to register"; read each row's onboarding_state to tell those apart). Omit to list all. Use linked before send_message, pending before verify/register.

phone_number.description: Optional: look up ONE number directly, in E.164 or any format (e.g. "+18525553623"). Takes precedence over waba_id and business_id, and is the only form that works on a business with too many accounts to list. Use it to answer "does this number exist yet" — in particular after an add that timed out, before retrying and creating a duplicate.

after.description: Optional: read the next page of accounts. Pass the next_after value from the previous result; its absence means there are no more. Only page when the user wants the whole list -- to find ONE number, pass phone_number, which resolves it directly however many accounts the business has.

shared_after.description: Optional: read the next page of numbers on customers' accounts shared with this business as their partner. Pass the shared_next_after value from the previous result; the call then returns only those shared numbers.

result.description: Paged: count is this page, total_whatsapp_accounts is the whole scope -- quote the total, never count, when telling the user how many they have. When total_whatsapp_accounts is absent and more_than_this_page is true, there is no count: say the list is partial and give no number, not even a floor. next_after carries the cursor for the next page when more exist. JSON-encoded list of phone numbers (phone_number_id, phone_number, name, status, onboarding_state, next_action). onboarding_state is registered, verified_not_registered, or not_verified; next_action is the one tool to call to move that number forward. A phone_number lookup also returns whatsapp_account_id, business_id, and the accounts linked to that WhatsApp Account. When that list is empty the response also carries incomplete and incomplete_reason: the account was created but never linked, and cannot send until it is.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_subscribe_webhook
tools.description: Subscribe an app to a WhatsApp Business Account's webhooks so it receives message and status events. Identify the account with waba_id or phone_number_id; or omit both and pass business_id (or rely on the selected business) — the tool uses the business's WhatsApp account if it has exactly one, otherwise it returns the list to choose from. The app is the event receiver: pass app_id, or omit it to have the tool list the business's apps and ask which app should receive events. Subscribing is ADDITIVE — it does not replace apps already subscribed to that WhatsApp account, and a WhatsApp account may have several subscribed apps, all of which receive every event. So if the user wants two or more apps receiving events, simply call this once per app; do NOT tell them it is one-app-only or that they must fan out events themselves. Webhook delivery needs THREE things, and this tool provides one: (1) WHICH WhatsApp account sends events -- set here; (2) WHERE they go -- the app's HTTPS callback URL and verify token, via whatsapp_biz_configure_webhooks; (3) the app PUBLISHED -- an app in development mode may not be sent real webhooks. Missing (1) or (2) delivers nothing, so never report webhooks as working off this call alone. To CHECK the current webhook state without changing it, call whatsapp_biz_onboarding_status -- this tool SUBSCRIBES, it is not an inspection tool, and calling it to look would silently create a subscription. Requires user confirmation. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter". This server has no undo: nothing here can unregister a number, remove a subscription, delete an account or reverse a write. Use the exact links returned by whatsapp_biz_onboarding_status in manage_links -- do not write those URLs from memory. Do not raise any of this unless asked.

waba_id.description: The WhatsApp business account id to subscribe to. This is the WhatsApp account that owns templates and billing (called a Messaging Account under WAME, but the same numeric id). Provide this or phone_number_id.

phone_number_id.description: A phone number id whose account to subscribe to. Used when waba_id is not given.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_send_message
tools.description: BEFORE calling this tool, make sure the user has picked a business (call whatsapp_biz_businesses if not done yet in this conversation). Send a WhatsApp message from a registered WhatsApp Business phone number. PREREQUISITE: whatsapp_biz_register_phone_number. Ask the user which kind to send and set message_type: 'text' is a free-form message that is ONLY delivered if the recipient messaged this business within the last 24 hours; to reach anyone else (or start a conversation), use 'template' with an APPROVED template. A number onboarded through this server starts with no templates at all, so if the user wants to send a template, create one first with whatsapp_biz_create_template and wait for it to be APPROVED. The resolved target is confirmed with the user before sending. Actions: send. OPTIMIZED DELIVERY -- ESTABLISH THE GOAL FIRST. Optimized delivery (a maximum delivery price, or a budgeted campaign) is set up on a template, never on an individual message. When the request only names pricing, bidding, a maximum price, a campaign, a budget or "better delivery" without saying what to do with it, ASK which of these three the user wants, in ONE question, before calling anything: (1) SET UP a template -- whatsapp_biz_create_template, with optimization_spec only if they want it; (2) OPTIMIZE a template that ALREADY exists, or change or remove the optimization it carries -- whatsapp_biz_update_template, which is also the only way to change what a template bids, never a second template; (3) USE a template that is already optimized and approved -- whatsapp_biz_send_message. Do NOT ask when the goal is already explicit: "create a template", "add a maximum price to template X", "send template X to this number" each name one, so proceed with it. Standard setup and optimization are two steps of one flow, not two different templates: the content is composed and confirmed the same way either way, and optimization is the optional optimization_spec on top. AN ALREADY-OPTIMIZED TEMPLATE SENDS LIKE ANY OTHER: message_type='template' with its name and language. The maximum price or campaign lives on the template, so there is no pricing, budget or campaign argument here and none is needed -- do not create a second template for the send, and do not re-run the optimization edit first. Prerequisites are checked before anything is sent: the template has to exist on the account the sending number belongs to and be APPROVED, and a template in any other state is refused naming that state -- the fix is to wait for review or edit the template, never to retry the send unchanged. The result also says when the account has no payment method or its review state puts delivery at risk; pass that on rather than promising the message will arrive. Never quote the bid or budget on the template as what the send will cost, and never predict a delivery rate, a cost per delivery or a reach figure. To change what the template bids, use whatsapp_biz_update_template. Public test numbers are deliberately left out of every list this server returns, and cannot be used to send. If the user asks about a test number, or about the test WhatsApp account it sits on, tell them it is for testing only: it reaches nobody except the recipients on its own allow-list, and that allow-list can only be managed on the app's WhatsApp API testing page in the Meta App Dashboard. Never offer to add a recipient to it or to send from it -- neither is possible from here.

to.description: Recipient phone number in E.164 format -- who the message goes to, as opposed to phone_number_id, which is who it is sent from. Must come from the user; never invent or guess a recipient.

message_type.description: What to send: 'text' or 'template'. 'text' (free-form) is ONLY delivered if the recipient messaged this business in the last 24 hours. That window is a delivery rule, not a pricing one: it applies to free-form text either way, and a payment method does not lift it. 'template' (an approved template) is delivered anytime. Either kind needs a payment method on the WhatsApp account: without one the message is still accepted by the API but the recipient most likely never sees it, so warn the user and point them at whatsapp_biz_configure_payments. Do not volunteer rates, or describe any message kind or template category as free or cheap, and never let cost influence which category a template is created under (see whatsapp_biz_create_template). If the user does ask what messages cost, answer them -- from the published rates at https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing, not from memory, since what is billable changes. Defaults to 'text'.

message.description: The message text. Required when message_type is 'text'. Reminder: free-form text only reaches recipients who messaged you within the last 24h.

category.description: Optional, for message_type 'text' only. Omit it unless this tool's description offers a category for this send.

template_name.description: Approved template name. Required when message_type is 'template'. Take it from the user -- most already know which template they want; only when they do not, use whatsapp_biz_list_templates so they can pick one. Either way, call whatsapp_biz_get_template on the chosen template and read its components before sending: APPROVED means WhatsApp accepted the template, not that this tool can send it. This tool fills body placeholders (body_parameters), a media, location or text header (header_parameter), and URL, quick reply and copy code button values (button_parameters). A template that needs any other value, such as a carousel, a limited time offer or a flow button token, has to go through the business's own Cloud API integration, which takes full components -- tell the user that, and do not offer to send it here.

language_code.description: Template language code (e.g. en_US). Required when message_type is 'template'.

body_parameters.description: JSON array of strings filling the template body placeholders {{1}}, {{2}}, ... in order -- e.g. ["Alice","12345"], which shows the format, not values to copy. Every value must come from the user or from real business data: never invent one, and never reuse the example values stored on the template, which exist for template review and are not real. Ask the user for any placeholder you cannot source. Omit only if the template body has no variables. Header and button values go in header_parameter and button_parameters; check the template components with whatsapp_biz_get_template first.

header_parameter.description: JSON object with the header value, for a template whose header is media, location or text with a {{1}}. Image, video or document: {"type":"image","link":"https://..."} with a public link to the file; a document can add "filename". Text: {"type":"text","text":"..."}. Location: {"type":"location","latitude":37.48,"longitude":-122.15,"name":"...","address":"..."}. The same rule as body_parameters applies: every value comes from the user or real business data, never from the template examples. Omit it when the header has no value to fill.

button_parameters.description: JSON array with one object for each button that takes a value: {"index":0,"sub_type":"url","text":"order/123"} fills the {{1}} at the end of a URL button, {"index":1,"sub_type":"quick_reply","payload":"..."} sets the payload returned when a quick reply is tapped, and {"index":2,"sub_type":"copy_code","coupon_code":"SAVE10"} sets the code of a copy code button. index is the button position in the template, from 0. The same sourcing rule as body_parameters applies. Omit it when no button takes a value.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of the message to be sent, including the app it will be sent from (and, if the business has more than one app, the list to choose from) so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true to actually send.

alternative_id.description: Optional: when the confirmation lists apps to choose from, set this to the app id the user picked. The app is who the send is attributed to (webhook delivery, rate limits, message attribution). It does not change which account is billed: every app offered belongs to the same business, so they all resolve to the same messaging account. Requires confirm=true.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_delete_template
tools.description: Delete WhatsApp message templates (irreversible). Three ways to call it: (1) one template version -- pass template_id and template_name; the name is cross-checked against the id as a safety guard. (2) every language version of a name -- also set all_languages=true (template_id must be one of the name's versions). (3) several versions at once -- pass template_ids (1 to 100 ids, duplicates ignored) instead of template_id and template_name; if any id is not on this waba_id the whole call is refused before anything is deleted, and the result reports each id. PREREQUISITE: a waba_id and the id(s) (use whatsapp_biz_list_templates or whatsapp_biz_get_template to find them); pass the selected business_id so the request can be authorized. If you do not have the waba_id, call whatsapp_biz_accounts first to find or pick one. Actions: delete. Never write "waba_id" or "WABA" in anything the user reads, including when explaining what a call did or why a result looks wrong. Name the account instead, or call it "the account filter".

waba_id.description: The WhatsApp business account id the template belongs to (Messaging Account under WAME; same numeric id).

template_id.description: The id of the single template version to delete. Required unless template_ids is passed.

template_name.description: The name of the template to delete; cross-checked against template_id. When all_languages is true, every language version of this name is deleted. Required with template_id.

template_ids.description: Delete several template versions at once: 1 to 100 id strings, duplicates ignored. Use instead of template_id and template_name, not together with them.

business_id.description: Optional: the business the WhatsApp account belongs to. Pass the business_id the user selected so the request is authorized against their admin access to that business.

confirm.description: Confirmation gate. Omit (or false) on the first call: the tool returns a summary of what it will do so you can ask the user to confirm. Only after the user says yes, re-call with the SAME arguments plus confirm=true to delete the template.

all_languages.description: Optional. When true, delete every language version of template_name (template_id is still required and must be one of the name's versions). When false or omitted, only the single version identified by template_id is deleted.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_verify_business
tools.description: BEFORE calling this tool, make sure the user has picked a business (call whatsapp_biz_businesses if not done yet in this conversation). REPORTS whether a business has passed Business Verification, and returns a deep link to the Security Center. This tool does not start or change anything -- verification is done by the user in Security Center, where the documents are uploaded and reviewed. Use it to answer "is this business verified" and to hand over the link. whatsapp_biz_businesses already carries business_verified for every business at once, so prefer that when the question is about more than one. No app_id needed.

business_id.description: The business id to verify.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_template_library
tools.description: Browse the WhatsApp Template Library: pre-written UTILITY and AUTHENTICATION templates for common use cases (order updates, delivery notifications, appointment reminders, payment requests, one-time passcodes, and so on). CHECK HERE FIRST whenever the user wants a template for an ordinary business notification, and offer what you find before writing one from scratch with whatsapp_biz_create_template. Two reasons it is the better start: a library template that is used UNCHANGED can skip review and be usable straight away (the pre_approved field says which ones), and its wording and category are already settled, so it cannot be rejected or recategorised for content. Create one with whatsapp_biz_create_template_from_library. Write your own only when nothing in the library fits, or the user asks for something specific to their business. Show the user a few real options with their body text rather than a list of names. When you already know a template by its exact name, pass name to fetch just that one. Pass an optional waba_id to filter the catalogue to templates a specific account can use. Actions: list.

search.description: Free-text search over the template name and body -- the best single filter for "find me a template about X" (e.g. "delivery", "appointment", "payment reminder").

name.description: Filter: EXACT template name. Unlike search, which matches a substring of the name or body, this returns only the template whose name equals this value exactly, or an empty page when none matches. Use it when the user gives a precise library template name.

language.description: Filter: language code the template is written in, e.g. en_US. Library templates are per-language, so pass the language the user's customers read.

category.description: Filter: categories, any-match. UTILITY, AUTHENTICATION. The library carries no MARKETING templates.

topic.description: Filter: topics, any-match (e.g. ORDER_MANAGEMENT, PAYMENTS, CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK). Omit unless the user named one -- search is usually the better filter.

usecase.description: Filter: use cases, any-match (e.g. DELIVERY_UPDATE, PAYMENT_DUE_REMINDER).

limit.description: Max library templates to return in this page (optional).

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page (optional).

waba_id.description: Optional: the WhatsApp business account id (same numeric id as the Messaging Account under WAME) to filter the catalogue to. Pass it to return only entries that account can actually use. Omit it to browse before an account is picked: that hides entries gated to specific accounts, but can also surface entries this account cannot use, such as India-only ones.

pin.description: The 6-digit two-step-verification PIN. Omit it on the first call: accounts on the current account model do not use a PIN and one passed here is ignored. Supply it only after this tool has asked for one.

verification_code.description: The one-time code the user received.

tools.name: whatsapp_biz_configure_payments
tools.description: BEFORE calling this tool, make sure the user has picked a business (call whatsapp_biz_businesses if not done yet in this conversation). Check the payment status of WhatsApp Business Accounts and return a Billing Hub deep link for each. Pass phone_number_id to check the single account that number belongs to, or business_id (or omit to auto-detect) to see ALL accounts under the business with their payment status.
